subject: Capacity commitment scenarios and onboarding cadence for Orpheus Labs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Pereira <sofia.p@orpheuslabs.com>, Liam Chen <liam.chen@orpheuslabs.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity commitment scenarios and onboarding cadence for Orpheus Labs

Hi Sofia / Liam,

Thanks again for the time this morning — attached is a concise set of capacity scenarios and an activation cadence we think maps to Orpheus Labs' traffic profile and risk tolerance. High level first, then a proposed onboarding path.

Executive summary:
- Goal: give Orpheus Labs predictable throughput for low-latency chat + nightly batch embedding jobs while keeping a clear ramp path and failover to hosted variants.
- We mapped three commitment scenarios (Starter / Growth / Anchor) to typical throughput buckets and rollout risk.

Commitment scenarios (recommended):
1) Starter lane — Minimal committed baseline
   - Minimum guaranteed: 8 GPUs (H100-class recommended)
   - Use case: short-term canary + light production footprint; supports low-concurrency chat and small embedding batches.
   - Ramp: active in week 1; can burst to 16 GPUs for short windows (pre-configured burst credit).

2) Growth lane — Predictable production
   - Minimum guaranteed: 24 GPUs
   - Use case: steady production serving with moderate concurrency and medium-length contexts.
   - Ramp: 8 -> 24 over first 90 days (see cadence sheet). Includes 1 week of warm-up credits for KV cache priming.

3) Anchor lane — Scale & redundancy
   - Minimum guaranteed: 64 GPUs
   - Use case: high throughput, regional redundancy, and aggressive SLAs.
   - Ramp: staged across months 1–6 with pre-warmed pools and cross-region failover.

Operational notes:
- Billing: committed GPUs are invoiced monthly as a capacity reservation with a usage true-up model (we credit unused burst where appropriate).
- SLA: 99.9% availability on committed capacity; automated fallback to compatible hosted instance types if the reserved pool is constrained.
- Canary recommendation: spin a 4-GPU canary for 14 days to validate latency and model config before moving to Starter lane.
- Warm-up credits: we include cache-warmup and sample-token allowances to avoid cold-start cost during ramp.

Attachments: orpheus_dedicated_options_v3.pdf (proposal summary); activation_cadence_sheet.xlsx (detailed week-by-week ramp).

Next steps I suggest:
- You (Sofia) share procurement contact if not already on thread.
- Quick 30-min workshop the week of July 10 to finalize starting lane and set canary dates.
- If you want, I can sketch a 90-day KPIs list (latency P95, tokens/day, cache hit rate) to track during canary.

Happy to refine — tell me which scenario you want pricing numbers for (I can run a tight estimate and include DocuSign-ready terms).

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Capacity commitment scenarios and onboarding cadence for Orpheus Labs

Marissa — thanks for the clear breakdown. A few clarifications from our side before we lock into a lane:  

1) Reservation vs preemption: are the committed GPUs preemptible at any time? We need to understand true isolation guarantees.
2) Billing model: is the monthly invoice based solely on the committed floor with a separate per-token/throughput usage surcharge, or is usage fully included up to a cap? We need example math for Starter vs Growth.
3) GPU spec: your note says H100-class — can you confirm expected model throughput (tokens/sec) for our baseline Llama-derivative at 2k context? This will help our SRE size concurrency targets.
4) Canary ask: procurement would like a formal 2-week pilot contract (limited-term commitment) to evaluate before converting to a multi-month commit. Is that possible?

Also cc'ing procurement so they have visibility on terms/questions. If you can reply with numbers and a short canary term sheet we can circulate internally.

Thanks — Sofia
Sofia Pereira
Head of Platform Engineering | Orpheus Labs
sofia.p@orpheuslabs.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Pereira <sofia.p@orpheuslabs.com>, Liam Chen <liam.chen@orpheuslabs.com>
Cc: Orpheus Labs Procurement <procurement@orpheuslabs.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity commitment scenarios and onboarding cadence for Orpheus Labs

Thanks — great questions, answered inline below. I'm also attaching a short 2-week pilot term sheet you can hand to procurement.

1) Reservation vs preemption
   - Committed GPUs are non-preemptible within the reserved pool; customers can opt for soft-burst lanes that allow preemptible capacity for cost savings, but the committed baseline is isolated and SLA-backed.

2) Billing model
   - Monthly invoice has two parts: (a) reservation fee for committed GPUs (flat monthly capacity fee) and (b) usage overage or add-on (token/embedding units) if you exceed included thresholds.
   - Example (illustrative): Starter lane (8 GPUs) — reservation fee covers baseline throughput up to X tokens/day; overage billed at $Y per 1M tokens. Growth lane (24 GPUs) includes a larger included token allowance and reduced per-token overage. I will push a detailed line-item estimate to the Deal record after you confirm starter vs growth.

3) GPU spec & throughput (approximate)
   - H100-class, optimized for medium-length attention. For your Llama-derivative at 2k context we estimate ~1,200–1,600 tokens/sec per GPU under our serving runtime (with kv cache hit patterns typical of session-based chat). Exact numbers depend on quantization and sequence churn; we can run a short synthetic test during the canary to validate.

4) Pilot / 2-week canary
   - Yes — we offer a limited 14-day pilot on a small committed pool (4 GPUs) with a capped fee. If you convert to a Starter lane within 30 days of pilot end, we can credit up to 50% of the pilot fee against the first month of reservation.

Proposed canary schedule (example):
- Week of Jul 10: Provision 4 GPUs, model sync, basic perf tests
- Jul 11–24: Production shadow/low-traffic canary window
- Jul 25: Quick review call and decision point

Estimated pricing (back-of-envelope):
- 4-GPU pilot (2 weeks): $8k–$10k (includes warm-up credits and limited engineering hours)
- Starter lane (8 GPUs): $28k/month reservation fee (includes a token allowance; overage at $0.XX / 1M tokens)
- Growth lane (24 GPUs): $80k/month reservation fee (reduced overage)
- Anchor lane (64 GPUs): custom enterprise pricing; we can discuss discount tiers tied to multi-quarter commits.

Next steps I can take now:
- Drop exact line-item pricing into the deal page and send a DocuSign-ready term sheet for the 14-day pilot.
- Schedule the kickoff provisioning slot for Jul 10 (will need approval from SRE for H100 capacity; typical lead time is 10–14 business days).

If procurement would like the short pilot term sheet as a redlineable PDF I can send it this afternoon.

Cheers,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0147
